### 1. Context and scope

Students and staff search for rooms and equipment, create or modify reservations, and cancel reservations. Library staff manage rooms, opening hours, recurring block bookings, and utilisation reports. Kiosks outside rooms display the current and next reservation.

CLRS integrates with three existing systems:

- the university identity provider through SAML;
- facilities calendars through iCal feeds; and
- a read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database.

# Campus Library Reservation System  
## Architecture and Quality Plan

### 1. Context and scope

The Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS) replaces the existing study-room reservation tool for three university libraries. Students and staff must be able to search rooms by campus, capacity, equipment and time window; create, modify and cancel reservations; and receive reminders. Library staff must manage rooms, opening hours and recurring block bookings, while kiosks outside rooms display the current and next reservation. The system integrates with the university SAML identity provider, facilities iCal feeds and a read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database.

This design covers the first release and addresses the stated functional requirements FR-1 to FR-6 and quality requirements QR-1 to QR-6. It focuses on an architecture that can be implemented and operated by a small team, while supporting reliable reservation rules, integration with external systems, kiosk refresh, reporting and future campus onboarding.

The proposed architecture is a **hexagonal modular monolith**, with a framework-independent reservation domain at its centre and adapters for HTTP, databases, SAML, iCal, notifications and kiosks. It is deployed as one application unit, with a relational transactional database and asynchronous workers for notifications, calendar synchronisation and reporting.
